claims.statement: SaiLoR is a tool for conducting Systematic Literature Reviews (SLRs); a project is a project.json file (annotation schema + paper metadata) plus a sibling annotations/<paperId>/ folder (per-reviewer and consolidated annotation data), and the app renders each paper's PDF beside a schema-generated annotation form, writing annotations back to that split layout.

Per-paper annotation files under annotations/ are created lazily (only once a reviewer writes something for that paper) and deleted again if the tree becomes empty; a project saved in the old single-file shape still opens and is migrated to the split layout automatically on the next save, with no explicit migrate step.

A screening project names its per-paper files screening-consolidated.json / screening-<n>.json instead of consolidated.json / reviewer-<n>.json, so screening and annotation project files are distinguishable at a glance while sharing the same layout.

The web/browser build is discontinued at runtime: src/App.tsx's isTauri() gate shows a 'SaiLoR for the web has been discontinued — use the desktop app' notice and blocks all project-opening UI before any file picker or project state is reached; npm run dev shows only that discontinuation screen, and the Tauri desktop dev loop (make dev / npx tauri dev) is the only usable way to run the app.

getPlatform() returns a cached TauriAdapter when isTauri() is true and createUnsupportedAdapter() otherwise; the unsupported adapter exists only because store.ts reads getPlatform().getRecents() at module load before App renders, answers the few pre-gate reads (kind, getRecents, setWindowTitle, feedback stubs) for real, and is a Proxy that throws 'SaiLoR for the web is discontinued — use the desktop app.' on every other method, so App.tsx's gate blocks all project-opening UI before anything else is reachable.

The tech stack is React 19 + TypeScript 5.7, Zustand 5 with immer middleware, Zod validation, react-pdf 9 (pdf.js) rendering plus pdf-lib for mark export, a Tauri 2 desktop shell (Rust crate in src-tauri/ bridged via @tauri-apps/api), Vite 6 for the renderer, and Vitest 3 + jsdom for testing (plus cargo test for the shell and tauri-driver for probe e2e).

The npm scripts are dev (vite), build (tsc -b && vite build), test (vitest run), test:integration (vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts), typecheck (tsc -b --noEmit), check:wiki (node scripts/check-wiki-links.js), and scenario (vite-node samples/git-scenarios/cli.ts); there are no dev:electron, build:electron, or test:e2e scripts anymore — desktop dev/build go through the Makefile's npx tauri targets.

The default vitest run (npm test) excludes the integration suite (*.integration.test.{ts,tsx}), which spins up a real scratch git repo per test and is slow; it runs on its own via npm run test:integration using the standalone vitest.integration.config.ts (a separate config because mergeConfig would concat include lists and pull ~90 unit files in), and CI runs it as its own step in scripts/ci.sh.

The e2e suite is a tauri-driver probe, not Playwright: e2e/probe.test.mjs (node --test) launches the binary built by `make probe` (--no-bundle --features probe --config tauri.probe.conf.json) through tauri-driver on 127.0.0.1:4444 with SAILOR_PROBE_PROJECT=samples/project.example.json, polls the probe page's #log element, and asserts the PDF rendered (RENDER OK) and a path-traversal request was refused (-> 403).

scripts/ci.sh is the provider-agnostic CI pipeline and single source of truth for 'does the app build and pass its checks': install (npm ci, skippable with SKIP_INSTALL=1) → typecheck → wiki-link check → npm test → npm run test:integration → npm run build; packaging for release installers is npx tauri build (make build), with Linux bundles built in Docker (make docker-linux).

The Tauri shell (src-tauri/src/main.rs) registers the plugins (single-instance with focus_main, window-state SIZE|POSITION|MAXIMIZED, dialog, updater, and an slr-os plugin whose js_init_script sets window.__SLR_OS__ to process.platform-style names), denies webview permission requests, serves PDFs over the async slr-file:// scheme via protocol::serve, and its generate_handler registry is grouped by domain: project_*, annotations_*, feedback, pdf_*/text_*, paths_*, web_fetch, llm_*, ollama_*/localruntime_*/local_probe, ~40 git_* commands, update_*, and close_*.

The renderer talks to the shell through the SlrBridge interface (src/platform/bridge.ts), implemented by tauriBridge in src/platform/tauri.ts, which maps each channel:Name to a snake_case Tauri command name (command()), sends positional args as named fields, and TauriAdapter (extending DesktopAdapter) reassembles the split project files into whole-project text via assembleProject before handing them to loadProject.

The domain model in src/model/ is pure and unit-tested: schema.ts (AnnotationDef/ResolvedDef types, zod schemas, resolveSchema), annotations.ts (AnnotationValueTree, normalizeTree, makeInstance), project.ts (loadProject, serializeProject, splitProjectFiles, isLegacyProjectShape, assembleLegacyProjectJson, Paper/Project types), and validate.ts (required/type/enum/cardinality checks that skip unannotated papers rather than flag them).

The main Zustand+immer store (src/state/store.ts, useStore at L1205) owns project, papers, save, annotations, undo/redo including PDF marks, and the currentTree routing that selects the single-reviewer, per-reviewer, or Consolidation annotation tree; setFieldValue coalesces consecutive edits of one field into one undo step and addInstance/removeInstance manage repeatable group instances, each pushing its own undo entry.

The AI-assisted annotation flow is kept in a separate aiStore.ts with its own phase lifecycle; the only place it meets the main store is applyAiSuggestions/applyAiSuggestionsBatch, a planned-then-applied batch write that is one undo step, never overwrites the reviewer's already-answered fields (replacements only when the field still holds exactly what the AI checked), refuses consolidation/screening/seat-mismatch targets, and records aiUsage disclosure.

The multi-reviewer consolidation logic lives in src/consolidate/ as pure, unit-tested functions: align.ts (alignNode, alignableNodes for hierarchical non-crossing entry matching), apply.ts (growConsolidated), and the supporting similarity, metrics, disagreements, unanimous, and readiness modules.

The git integration's pure logic lives in src/git/merge.ts as mergeProjects and applyResolutions (the field-level three-way merge), with security gates in ref.ts (refProblem, isSafeRef), relpath.ts (relPathProblem, isSafeRelPath, annotationsRelDir), url.ts (validateGitUrl), and ownAnnotationPath.ts; the shell-side plumbing is src-tauri/src/git.rs, which mirrors those validators in Rust (rel_path_problem, ref_problem, and the URL scheme allowlist), and gitStore.ts stays the thin UI layer.

Screening mode is a derived two-node (Decision/Reason) schema (src/screening/schema.ts, isScreening) with a tri-state status read (screeningStatus: included/excluded/undecided), PRISMA-style counts (screeningCounts), and two cross-field validation rules (screeningIssues); it reuses the multi-reviewer/Consolidation machinery.

Native self-update is handled by tauri-plugin-updater driven from src-tauri/src/update.rs (update_check/update_download/update_install; AppImage/NSIS/MSI/App bundles only — deb/rpm report manual updates), with the feed URL and minisign pubkey configured in tauri.conf.json (requireSignedVersion: true) against the signed latest.json release asset; src/model/version.ts is the renderer-side GitHub-releases check that decides *whether* an update notice shows and store.ts's checkForUpdate only asks the native updater once that check has confirmed a newer version — there is no Ed25519 feed verifier in the renderer anymore (src/model/updateSignature.ts is gone).
